title: Array literal
summary: Proves that the compiler's array-literal template allocates an owned Array UInt64 holding the element values, keeps the allocator invariant, and keeps every borrowed array.
premises: The module has no imports, a 32-bit memory, and alloc at function 0
The destination local is below scratch and the state covers the scratch index
Heap.At, a memory cap of at most 65,535 pages, and 8 * (k + 1) at most 2^32
Each element expression evaluates to its word in every state framed from the start except the destination
result: The facts of Heap.NewArray for the new array: the allocator invariant, the owned array, every earlier region kept and apart from the new object, and the memory limits.
